{{MEinfobox
|name=Sinking
|cg=Sinking.png}}
{{StatusEffect|Sinking|d}} is a status effect that deals bonus Sanity (SP) damage to the afflicted unit. When hit, the unit with Sinking will take SP damage equal to the Sinking Potency, and Sinking Count will be reduced by 1. Units with no SP (such as Abnormalities) will take fixed {{Icons|Gloom}}Gloom damage equal to the Sinking Potency instead.

{{StatusEffect|Sinking|d}} is linked to the {{Icons|Gloom}}Gloom Sin Affinity.

==Strengths & Weaknesses==
{{StatusEffect|Sinking|d}} is a Status Effect that has two independent use conditions. Against enemies with Sanity, Sinking is a very effective method of making the fight easier, as lowering enemy SP tanks their ability to roll well (with the exception of enemies that use negative Coins). A Sinking team also quickly triggers "Low Morale" and "Panic" effects, which often cause debuffs such as {{StatusEffect|Fragile|d}}. Against enemies without Sanity, {{StatusEffect|Sinking|d}} behaves very similar to {{StatusEffect|Rupture|x}}[[Rupture]], having an extremely high damage cap. Because Sinking Potency has a maximum value of 99, a Sinking team can deal 99 fixed {{Icons|Gloom}}Gloom damage <u>per hit per turn</u>. For example, a team of 6 using only 2-Coin Skills could deal '''1188 {{Icons|Gloom}}Gloom damage per turn'''.  While it is very difficult to get Sinking Potency and Count high enough to deal that much damage outside of Mirror Dungeons, smaller amounts can still deal a lot of extra damage, especially against enemies with high level or other forms of damage reduction that take less damage from regular attacks. It is worth noting that damage caused by {{StatusEffect|Sinking|d}} will ignore Damage Type resistances, but not Sin resistances. The damage will be higher against enemies weak to {{Icons|Gloom}}Gloom and lower against enemies that are resistant.

{{StatusEffect|Sinking|d}} is generally effective against all groups of enemies, but is especially effective against enemies without SP, Abnormalities with only one Part, and positive-Coin Bosses with SP. Sinking Identities almost always have a {{Icons|Gloom}} Gloom skill. Sinking damage ignores damage reduction from buffs (like {{StatusEffect|Protection|b}}) and level scaling, but does not ignore enemy resistances / weaknesses to {{Icons|Gloom}} Gloom. {{StatusEffect|Sinking|d}} will deal double damage to Abnormalities that are Fatal to {{Icons|Gloom}} Gloom.

{{StatusEffect|Sinking|d}} is least effective against Abnormalities with multiple Parts, as it becomes difficult to build a high Sinking stack on a single Part. Using a Sinking team against enemies with SP that primarily use negative Coins is also not recommended, as the SP reduction effect simply makes their Skills more stable. {{StatusEffect|Sinking|d}} will deal less damage to Abnormalities that are Resistant to {{Icons|Gloom}} Gloom.

{{StatusEffect|Sinking|d}} teams tend to be slow in fights against large numbers of enemies with SP. This is because Sinking does not deal direct damage against enemies with SP. Despite this downside, the low SP of enemies will make winning clashes very easy, so it is up to the player to decide if they would prefer a faster team that can deal more damage or not. Both {{StatusEffect|Butterfly|d}} and {{StatusEffect|Sinking Deluge|d}} are effects that deal {{Icons|Gloom}}Gloom damage to enemies based on Sinking values, and they can be used to gradually pick off enemies, though this requires more management of Sinking stacks.

There are two main strategies for {{StatusEffect|Sinking|d}} teams. Against groups of enemies or enemies with low HP, a combination of {{StatusEffect|Sinking|d}}, {{StatusEffect|Butterfly|d}}, and Panic Type-changing Status Effects deal bonus HP and SP damage and allow attackers to gain SP on hit. Effects that change Panic Type, such as {{StatusEffect|Echoes of the Manor|d}}, also helps with Sinking infliction. <br>
Against single enemies with high HP (with several thousand HP or so), {{StatusEffect|Sinking Deluge|d}} is more powerful. Because Sinking Deluge deals damage equal to Sinking Potency * Sinking Count, it has the current highest damage potential in the game, totaling in at 99*99 = 9801 damage (before accounting for {{Icons|Gloom}}Gloom resistance). Currently, [[Effloresced E.G.O::Spicebush Yi Sang|Spicebush Yi Sang]] is the only Identity with {{StatusEffect|Sinking Deluge|d}}. It needs also to be noted that {{StatusEffect|Sinking Deluge|d}} is considered as direct hit damage for all purpose, unlike most damage related to Status effects. Thus, it can raise Observation Level, trigger [On Kill] effects and is taken into account for "Damage from a single skill use" achievements.

{{StatusEffect|Sinking|d}} and {{StatusEffect|Rupture|d}} differ slightly. Sinking Identities generally inflict more Sinking Count and less Potency when compared to Rupture Identities. This makes Sinking stacks easier to maintain, but the effects may take longer to build up than Rupture teams.

==Self-Sinking==
Although very uncommon, some Identities gain {{StatusEffect|Sinking|d}} when using their skills, and use Sinking Potency or Count as if it was {{StatusEffect|Charge|x}}[[Charge]] to improve the effectiveness of their skills. Sinking used in this way still functions as a debuff, meaning that fighting enemies that inflict {{StatusEffect|Sinking|d}} can either be dangerous or a convenient way to easily allow a self-Sinking Identity to function at maximum capacity quickly.
